problems.title: Persistent finite iterators exhaust during hybrid multi-epoch training
claim: The release constructs both finite loader iterators once before a requested multi-epoch alternating loop.
analysis: For two four-batch loaders, epoch zero consumes two batches from each and epoch one consumes the remaining two. Epoch two’s first video request raises StopIteration; only \(8\) updates occur despite the \(1000\)-epoch request. In general completion needs \(E\lceil L/2\rceil\le L_v\) and \(E\lfloor L/2\rfloor\le L_i\). Re-entering the outer loop does not renew exhausted iterator objects. This reasoning depends only on ordinary finite iterator semantics, not model or accelerator execution.
result: The released loop cannot generally perform its requested training schedule. Historical private training and published scores are not thereby proved wrong.
repair: Renew iterators at each epoch for the equal-length schedule; explicitly choose stopping/cycling/resampling for unequal lengths and define whether an epoch is a full pass through either dataset.
problems.impact_rationale: A concrete training-release defect prevents faithful multiepoch execution, without refuting model capability or reported checkpoint quality.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Mask filling changes when unrelated frames are duplicated
claim: The conditioning expression uses per-frame/channel spatial numerators divided by total mask area across every flattened frame.
analysis: For \(N\) identical constant frames of value \(c\) with common nonempty mask area \(a\), each numerator is \(ca\) and the denominator is \(Na\); masked fill becomes \(c/N\). With \(c=1\), duplication changes fill from \(1\) to \(1/2\), even though the original pixels and mask are unchanged. Unmasked pixels are preserved. The paper does not require a per-frame-mean filling rule, so unintended semantics cannot be concluded from this dependency alone.
result: Cross-frame and frame-count dependence is exact, but whether it violates intended conditioning remains unresolved. No poorer temporal or identity score is inferred.
problems.impact_rationale: The numerical dependency is proved; the manuscript lacks a fill-rule contract establishing that this is an unintended error.
problems.existing_correction_status: No applicable author correction was established in this inspection.

problems.title: Video-level retrieval percentages require a denominator clarification
claim: The protocol states \(200\) generated videos and temporal average cosine comparisons, while reporting Top-1 \(78.3\%\) and Top-5 \(90.2\%\).
analysis: If each video produces one binary ranked result, accuracy lies on multiples of \(100/200=0.5\) percentage points; neither printed value is attainable, including one-decimal rounding. But framewise ranking over \(200\times128=25600\) frames has spacing \(0.00390625\) points, and \(20045\) successes gives \(78.30078125\%\). Repeats, exclusions or different pairing counts could likewise explain finer increments.
result: The direct one-rank-per-video reading is incompatible with the table, but the actual hidden metric convention is unresolved. No replacement accuracy is justified.
problems.impact_rationale: Alternative plausible trial units resolve the arithmetic; original evaluator and run counts are needed.
problems.existing_correction_status: No applicable author correction was established in this inspection.

problems.title: The sample demo is not the full benchmark protocol
claim: The paper evaluates \(128\)-frame videos with \(32\) DDIM steps; the README sample demo caps frame length at \(80\) and requests \(40\) steps.
analysis: A \(128\)-frame input remains divisible by \(8\), then the source cap yields \(80\) frames. The pipeline explicitly receives \(40\) inference steps. The README calls this a sample test, so a separate benchmark implementation could use the published settings.
result: This limits reproduction through the demo rather than disproving a paper result. A matching evaluator needs explicit frame cap, steps, checkpoint and metric configuration.
problems.impact_rationale: A disclosed sample command need not itself implement the complete benchmark protocol.
problems.existing_correction_status: No applicable author correction was established in this inspection.

impact_rationale: Minor: a bounded current training-code defect is supported; other concerns retain uncertainty and sample-demo qualifications.
